heuristics.statement: Algebraic interpolation attack on 11-round Poseidon. The output polynomial has degree D ≈ 5^11 ≈ 5×10^6. Interpolation requires D+1 evaluations (2^{30.4} operations). Collision finding uses fast root-finding algorithms on the interpolated polynomial, achieving complexity 2^{90} operations, a 38-bit improvement over the generic birthday bound of 2^{128}.
heuristics.scope: Time estimate based on algebraic attack complexity. Requires polynomial interpolation and fast root-finding.
heuristics.extrapolation: Degree growth analysis: 8 full rounds multiply degree by 5^8, 3 partial rounds multiply by 5^3, giving total degree ≈ 5^11. Interpolation cost is linear in degree. Collision search uses algebraic structure to beat birthday bound.
heuristics.limitations: The 2^{90} complexity is a conservative estimate based on algebraic attack theory. Actual complexity depends on the efficiency of polynomial arithmetic and root-finding implementations. The attack requires sophisticated algebraic geometry techniques.
